newsitem.title: USA: Quaker expects second half share buybacks.
newsitem.headline: Quaker expects second half share buybacks.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Thursday it expects to buy back shares in the second half of 1997 under an existing share repurchase authorization.
"We do expect to buy back shares in the second half," William Smithburg, chairman, told a teleconference.
Quaker has existing authorization to buy back about 3.4 million shares, he said.
Earlier this year Quaker said it would resume share repurchases that were suspended in the summer of 1994.
Smithburg also said Quaker's board was making progress in its search for his successor. He gave no details on when his successor might be named.

In April Smithburg said he planned to step down after 16 years as chairman and chief executive officer. He has been criticized for purchasing Snapple beverages in December 1994 in a $1.8 billion deal. Earlier this year Quaker took a one-time charge of $1.14 billion and sold the business for $300 million.
Quaker today reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings.
"Overall, we're very pleased with this quarter," Smithburg said.
Quaker Oats shares at midday were up 7/8 at 46.
